Done — narrow patch only.

## `render_scene.py`

Deleted the speculative wrapper (`_param_same`, `_blender_version`, `_set_node_param`) and rewrote the Glare setup as direct Blender 4.5 calls:

```python
glare.glare_type = "FOG_GLOW"
glare.quality = "HIGH"
glare.inputs["Threshold"].default_value = 0.7
glare.inputs["Size"].default_value = 0.5      # normalised socket, not legacy size=7
```

A wrong socket name now raises `KeyError` from Blender itself — no version abstraction, no read-back probing, no swallowed warnings. `0.7` was kept for the threshold (socket default 1.0); `Size` moved from the legacy integer 7 to the normalised 0.5 exactly as instructed.

## `tests/test_render_geometry.py`

Removed the whole `TestGlareHelper` class (4 tests — the two that failed plus the two that mirrored the now-deleted wrapper) and removed `test_idle_boards_stay_dark` (the scalar `IDLE_BOARD[i]` sum). No other test touched, none weakened. What remains is behavioral: axis conversion, board/posts/ground geometry, derived-vs-fixed floor with the 700-note case, orthographic framing (4–6 boards, ball small and near centre, whole ball inside the frame through the hop), and the saturated-palette check on `glow_color` output.

Camera, lighting, palette, motion and timing constants were **not** altered in this patch — the only renderer edit is the Glare block.

It also says explicitly that I ran no tests and no renders.
